title: Drummers Roy, Joe Rena and Chinee's stick tricks
summary: He recalls drummers with Sam Morgan and Kid Rena; Chinee twirled sticks and sang into his snare drum.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Were there any other early drummers that you can remember when you were a boy?

Well, let's see, there was a, there was a fellow by the name of Roy, he used to play with Sam Morgan, Sam Morgan's band. I don't know if that is his last name, but he was a wonderful little drummer. His name was Roy, and he had one who used to play with Kid Rainey, his brother, his name was Rainey, but I never knew it was Joe Rainey. But when Joe Rainey was with his brother, he was another wonderful drummer.
It's not far from here, he's down on Jackson, he's a preacher now, works in the church. Yeah, Joe's the Witness.
Well, those two, Chani, I mentioned him, he was a wonderful little drummer.
Did Chani do any tricks with his sticks?
Yeah, he used to do, he would, he used to throw them up in the air. Oh yeah. Throw them up in the air and catch them, play them, twirl them on his fingers. He was a wonderful guy.

We talked to him a few months ago, he had one thing he puts on hitting the sticks together, sort of holding them up here and rolling them, you know, so one hand hits them in the other end. Did you ever see him do that in the old days?
I used to see him, yeah, I used to see him hold them in the trees and hit them on the sticks. Yeah, I used to watch him do that thing.
And did he have some way of singing with his snare drum?
Yeah, he used to hold the snare drum up to his mouth and sing to it.
Well, did he have his mouth against the head of the snare?
Against the head of the snare drum, right to his mouth when he would sing, and you could hear the vibration.
Right on the skin. Right on the skin.
And you could hear the vibration from the drum while he was singing. That was wonderful. I forgot about that. That was one of the things he used to hold the drum.
